title: Equivariant evaluation after normal domination and integral curve base change
statement:
Let $k$ be a field, $S$ a normal integral projective finite-type $k$-scheme with function field $L$, and $(W\to S,s_i)$ an H-projective stable pointed curve with smooth geometrically integral generic fibre. Let $Q\to S$ be H-projective and suppose every morphism $\mathbf P^1_\Omega\to Q_\Omega$ is constant for every algebraically closed geometric residue field $\Omega$. Let a finite group $J$ act compatibly on $k,S,W,Q$, preserving the union of markings, and let $u_\eta:W_\eta\to Q_\eta$ be an equivariant generic morphism.

There are an integral projective birational morphism $R\to S$ with a $J$-action, an equivariant evaluation $W_R\to Q_R$ extending $u_\eta$, a normal integral projective finite-type $k$-scheme $S'$, a finite group $J'$ with a surjection $\rho:J'\to J$, an equivariant H-projective alteration $S'\to S$, and an equivariant $S$-morphism $S'\to R$. The extension $L'=k(S')/L$ is finite separable and $(L')^{\ker\rho}=L$. Pulling evaluation and the sections back gives a $J'$-equivariant morphism $W_{S'}\to Q_{S'}$ and an H-projective stable pointed curve over $S'$.

More generally, for every integral scheme $T$ and dominant morphism $T\to S$, the scheme $W_T$ is integral and its generic fibre is smooth geometrically integral. If $L_T=k(T)$ is finite over $L$ and $D=k(W)$, the natural generic map identifies $k(W_T)=D\otimes_L L_T$; this tensor algebra is a field, with its natural compatible group actions whenever the base change is equivariant. These integrality and finite-extension field conclusions also hold after any subsequent dominant integral base change of this family, including finite purely inseparable changes. Here birational means isomorphism over a dense open; $Q$ need not be integral or flat. Tensor products use [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product], with the algebra multiplication $(d\otimes a)(d'\otimes a')=dd'\otimes aa'$.

Field, integrality, properness, finite type, geometric integrality, dimension, H-projectivity, finite morphisms, surjectivity, function fields and field extensions use [def-weil-field], [def-pc-integral-scheme], [def-weil-proper-morphism], [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible], [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension], [def-kun-projective], [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism], [def-weil-surjective-morphism], [def-sc-function-field], [def-pc-field-extension] and [def-pc-field-tower]. H-projective means a closed immersion into a finite-dimensional projective space over the target. Normal means all local rings are integrally closed domains. An alteration is a proper surjective morphism of integral schemes, with finite function-field extension and finite over a dense open. Actions may be nonfaithful and semilinear on the ground field; equivariance through a group surjection always includes its action on that field. Purely inseparable means every element has a characteristic-power in the smaller field in positive characteristic, and equality in characteristic zero. Flatness, finite presentation, smoothness, geometric fibres, closed immersions and fibre products use [def-weil-flat-morphism], [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], [def-weil-geometric-fibre], [def-weil-closed-immersion] and [def-pc-fibre-product]. Stable pointed curve means [def-sfb-stable-pointed-curve]; its sections may be permuted. Quasi-split means [def-sfb-quasi-split-nodal-fibres].

proof.text: By [def-sfb-stable-pointed-curve], the given $W/S$ is flat and finitely presented with nonempty connected reduced nodal geometric curve fibres. Its H-projectivity and smooth geometrically integral generic fibre are hypotheses. Thus [lem-sfb-high-genus-hom-closure] applies to $(S,W,Q,u_\eta)$: its rational-curve exclusion is exactly our hypothesis on each geometric fibre of $Q$, and it requires neither flatness nor integrality of $Q$. Obtain the integral H-projective birational $R\to S$ and its evaluation $e:W_R\to Q_R$. The naturality clause supplies the $J$-action on $R$ and equivariance of $e$, including the given semilinear action on $k$.

source.place: §§3.9--3.13, printed p.609; publisher PDF read online at https://aif.centre-mersenne.org/item/10.5802/aif.1575.pdf (local copy WANTED)

proof.text: Identify $k(R)=L$ by the dense-open isomorphism $R\to S$. Let $\nu:S'\to R$ be normalization in this same field $L$. Apply [lem-sfb-finite-normalization-model-functoriality] with $V=R$, $H=M=L$: $R$ is integral finite type over $k$, by [lem-pc-projective-proper] (H-projective implies proper), [def-weil-proper-morphism] (proper includes finite type) and [lem-sfb-finite-type-composition-base-change]. The lemma gives normal integral finite-type $S'$, finite surjective $\nu$, $k(S')=L$, and a compatible $J$-action on $S'$ from that on $R,L$. Its identity/composition clause verifies the group law even for a nonfaithful action and a nontrivial action on $k$.

source.place: Tags 0307 (lemma-integral-closure-localize), 034L (lemma-integral-closure-in-normal); finite semilinear normalization as stated in the cited node

proof.text: By [lem-trf-h-projective-composition], $R/k$ is H-projective. Its projective-space embedding therefore supplies an ample invertible sheaf by [lem-weil-pbc-projective-ample-invertible], applied over the affine base $\operatorname{Spec}k$. The finite morphism $\nu$ is projective in the projective-bundle sense by [lem-trf-finite-projective-bundle]; since its target $R$ has this ample sheaf, [lem-trf-projective-bundle-to-h-projective] makes $\nu$ H-projective. Composition makes both $S'\to S$ and $S'\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ H-projective. By [lem-pc-projective-proper], $S'\to S$ is proper. The generic point of $S'$ maps to that of $S$, since their function fields are identified with $L$, so the image is dense. By [def-weil-proper-morphism], properness includes universal closedness; its identity base change is a closed map. Applying this to the closed set $S'$ makes the image closed, hence all of $S$.

source.place: Tags 01WE (lemma-H-projective-composition), 0B3I (lemma-finite-projective), 087S (lemma-projective-over-quasi-projective-is-H-projective); ample sheaf on a projective scheme as in the cited node

proof.text: Choose a dense open $U\subset S$ on which $R\to S$ is an isomorphism. Replacing $U$ by $\bigcap_{j\in J}jU$ makes it $J$-stable; this finite intersection is still dense open because $S$ is irreducible. Normalization commutes with restriction by [lem-sfb-finite-normalization-model-functoriality]. Over $U$ it is normalization of the normal scheme $U$ in its own function field: its integral-closure sheaf has the same stalks as the original sheaf, since each local ring is integrally closed in $L$. Hence this restriction is the identity by [def-fin-normalization-extension]. Thus $S'\to S$ is an isomorphism, in particular finite, over $U$. Together with step 3 this is an alteration as defined in the statement. Set $J'=J$ and $\rho=\mathrm{id}_J$. Then $L'=k(S')=L$ is a finite separable extension of degree one, and $(L')^{\ker\rho}=L$. The required map $S'\to R$ is $\nu$, already equivariant.

source.place: Tag 0307 (lemma-integral-closure-localize); normalization in the original fraction field of a normal domain

proof.text: Pull $e$ and every marking back along $S'\to R\to S$. The universal property [def-pc-fibre-product] gives the evaluation $W_{S'}\to Q_{S'}$; composing with the two projections shows it agrees with $u_\eta$ on the generic fibre. The arbitrary-base-change clause of [lem-sfb-stable-pointed-generic-extension] says the stable pointed conditions persist. H-projectivity persists by [lem-pc-projective-base-change]. The diagonal action sends $(w,t)$ to $(jw,jt)$, so both projections and the pulled-back evaluation are equivariant. For each marking $s_i$, the identity $j s_i=s_{j(i)}j$ pulls back to the identical equation for the new marking. Hence its union is preserved.

source.place: §§3.9--3.13, printed p.609; publisher PDF read online at https://aif.centre-mersenne.org/item/10.5802/aif.1575.pdf (local copy WANTED)

proof.text: Let $T\to S$ be any dominant morphism with $T$ integral; no Noetherian or finite-type hypothesis is imposed on $T$. Write $N=k(T)$. Its generic point maps to $\eta$, so the generic fibre of $X=W_T\to T$ is $W_\eta\times_L N$, by [def-pc-fibre-product]. It is smooth by the smooth clause of [lem-pc-proper-base-change], and geometrically integral by [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible]: further extension to any field over $N$ is the same extension of $W_\eta$. In particular it is nonempty. The morphism $X\to T$ is flat by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-morphism-base-change].

source.place: Tag 01U9 (lemma-base-change-flat); smooth base change Tag 01VB (lemma-base-change-smooth); geometric integrality under field extension by its definition

proof.text: For a nonempty affine chart $V=\operatorname{Spec}B\subset X$ mapping into an affine $U=\operatorname{Spec}A\subset T$, $A$ is a domain with fraction field $N$ by [lem-sc-integral-function-field-affine-fraction]. By [lem-weil-pbc-flat-morphism-affine-criterion] and [lem-trf-flat-module-torsionfree-domain], $B$ is flat and torsion-free over $A$. Thus $B\to (A\setminus\{0\})^{-1}B=B\otimes_A N$ is injective: an element killed by localization is killed by a nonzero element of $A$. The localized ring is nonzero since $B\ne0$, and it is the ring of the corresponding affine open of $X_N$ by [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra]. Since $X_N$ is integral, it is a domain, hence so is $B$. These charts cover $X$, so $X$ is reduced. Every nonempty open of $X$ contains such a chart and therefore meets $X_N$. Any two nonempty opens meet in $X_N$, since $X_N$ is irreducible; hence $X$ is irreducible. With nonemptiness from step 6, [def-pc-integral-scheme] gives integrality of $W_T$, including $T=S$.

source.place: Tag 01U5 (lemma-flat-characterize); affine generic-fibre calculation using Schemes Tag 01JQ and flat-module torsion-freeness

proof.text: Put $D=k(W)$, now defined because step 7 with $T=S$ proves $W$ integral. Choose nonempty affine opens $\operatorname{Spec}B\subset W$ and $\operatorname{Spec}A\subset S$ with the first mapping into the second. Set $C=B\otimes_A L=(A\setminus\{0\})^{-1}B$. It is a nonzero affine coordinate ring in $W_\eta$ by [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra]. By [lem-sc-integral-function-field-affine-fraction], $D=\operatorname{Frac}B=\operatorname{Frac}C$: localizing a domain at nonzero elements does not change its fractions. For every extension $N/L$, $C\otimes_L N$ is the coordinate ring of a nonempty affine open in $W_\eta\times_L N$, hence a domain by [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible] and the same affine fibre-product formula.

source.place: Tag 01JQ (lemma-fibre-product-affines); Morphisms Tag 01RV (lemma-integral-scheme-rational-functions); geometric integrality definition

proof.text: Now assume $N=L_T$ finite over $L$. Tensor bilinearity [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product] identifies $D\otimes_L N$ with $(C\setminus\{0\})^{-1}(C\otimes_L N)$: send $(c/s)\otimes a$ to $(c\otimes a)/(s\otimes1)$, with inverse obtained from $c\otimes a\mapsto c\otimes a$ and inversion of $s\otimes1$. These formulas respect multiplication and the tensor relations and are inverse on the indicated generators. The elements $s\otimes1$ are nonzero because scalar extension is injective on $L$-vector spaces: a basis of $C$ extends the nonzero vector $s$, so $s\otimes1$ is nonzero in that extended basis. Thus the tensor algebra is a nonzero domain by step 8. A finite $L$-basis $(a_i)$ of $N$ gives the finite $D$-spanning set $(1\otimes a_i)$, so [lem-weil-pbc-finite-dimensional-domain-is-field] makes it a field. For a nonempty affine $\operatorname{Spec}A_T\subset T$ mapping into $\operatorname{Spec}A$, the pulled-back affine chart has ring $B\otimes_A A_T$ and generic ring $C\otimes_L N$ by [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra]. Localizing this domain at $A_T\setminus\{0\}$ leaves its fraction field unchanged; [lem-sc-integral-function-field-affine-fraction] therefore gives $k(W_T)=\operatorname{Frac}(C\otimes_L N)$. Since the displayed localization is already a field, it equals that fraction field. This proves the canonical identification $k(W_T)=D\otimes_L L_T$ induced by the generic maps.

source.place: Tag 00CV (section-tensor-product), tensor universal property and explicit localization maps; finite-dimensional domain field criterion (rank-nullity) as in the cited node

proof.text: For an equivariant base change, a group element acts on the tensor algebra by $d\otimes a\mapsto g(d)\otimes g(a)$. This is balanced since the two actions agree on $L$, and it preserves multiplication by the stated pure-tensor formula. The two maps in step 9 send these expressions to the same generic rational function, so the field identification is equivariant. After any further dominant integral base change the family is again flat with smooth geometrically integral generic fibre by step 6. Repeat steps 7--9 over that new integral base; step 7 has no finiteness assumption, and step 9 only needs the new extension to be finite. No argument used separability of that extension. Consequently finite purely inseparable extensions are included, as are all successive dominant integral changes for integrality. The action and projection compatibilities follow on pure tensors and pairs, using [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product] and [def-pc-fibre-product].

source.place: Tag 00CV (section-tensor-product); agent verification on pure tensors of semilinear compatibility and iteration
